extra.message: POST /search interpolates request.json['search'] into a quoted SQL expression and executes it through db.engine.execute(). An authenticated attacker can terminate the string and inject UNION queries to extract database contents, including credentials.

The 404 handler interpolates attacker-controlled request.url into template source before calling render_template_string(). An unauthenticated request to a nonexistent URL containing Jinja expressions causes server-side evaluation, enabling configuration disclosure and arbitrary Python code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The /search exception handler interpolates str(e) into Jinja template source. Database exceptions include the SQL statement containing attacker-controlled search input. A malformed query containing Jinja expressions therefore reaches render_template_string(), allowing an authenticated attacker to execute server-side template expressions and arbitrary Python code.

extra.message: Unauthenticated POST /yaml_hammer reads an uploaded file and passes its contents to yaml.load() without SafeLoader. The pinned PyYAML 3.12 defaults to the unrestricted Loader, allowing Python object construction and callable invocation through malicious YAML tags, resulting in remote code execution. See [PyYAML 3.12 loader selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaml/pyyaml/3.12/lib/yaml/__init__.py).

Unauthenticated POST /xxe_uploader passes an attacker-supplied DOCX to Document() without disabling external entities. The pinned python-docx 0.8.5 parser leaves entity resolution enabled. A document containing a local-file external entity in its final paragraph can disclose server files through para.text, which is returned at line 308. See [python-docx parser configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-openxml/python-docx/v0.8.5/docx/oxml/__init__.py).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: insecure_verify() decodes JWTs with verify=False and returns True whenever decoding succeeds. GET /get/<cust_id> uses this function as its authentication check. An attacker can submit a fabricated token without a valid signature and retrieve customer records, including credit-card numbers.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The JWT signing key is hardcoded as 'secret'. login() signs HS256 tokens with this key, and verify_jwt() trusts it. Anyone knowing or guessing this value can forge accepted tokens and bypass authentication on /fetch/customer and /search.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: First-request initialization creates the admin account with the hardcoded password 'admin123'. This credential also exists in the bundled app/test.db. An unauthenticated attacker can submit these credentials to /login and receive a valid access token.

login() compares the supplied password directly against the database password column without password-hash verification. setup_users() persists the administrator password unchanged, and the bundled database contains that plaintext value. Database disclosure therefore immediately exposes usable credentials.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: POST /login prints the complete request JSON before authentication. This includes the submitted username and plaintext password, exposing credentials in process and container logs for both successful and failed login attempts.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The 404 page inserts request.url directly into HTML template source without escaping. In the pinned Werkzeug version, URL decoding restores encoded HTML metacharacters. A crafted nonexistent URL can therefore inject script or event-handler markup into the HTML response and execute JavaScript in a visitor's browser. See [Werkzeug 0.14.1 URL decoding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pallets/werkzeug/0.14.1/werkzeug/urls.py).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

extra.message: POST /search returns raw database exception text to the requester. Malformed search input exposes SQL statements, database error details, and internal table and column names, providing information useful for further injection attacks.

extra.message: Unauthenticated /xxe_uploader saves every uploaded file into Files/ before validating its contents, with no storage quota or cleanup. /yaml_hammer repeats this at line 324. Repeated uploads with distinct filenames remain on disk even when parsing fails, allowing an attacker to exhaust server storage.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: POST /xxe_uploader opens an untrusted DOCX archive without checking decompressed sizes or compression ratios. Document() reads ZIP members fully into memory, so a small upload containing highly compressed, oversized document parts can exhaust memory and CPU. See [python-docx ZIP member reading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-openxml/python-docx/v0.8.5/docx/opc/phys_pkg.py).

cwe: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data

extra.message: The application starts an HTTPServer without TLS and listens on the exposed application port. The supplied Docker workflow publishes this port directly, and the test client uses HTTP. In this supplied deployment, login passwords, bearer tokens, and returned customer credit-card data travel unencrypted and can be intercepted by a network attacker.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The workflow starts ZAP on 0.0.0.0:8090, accepts API clients matching '.*', and explicitly disables the API key.
